summary: Microsoft's MAI-Code-1.1-Flash card describes a dedicated coding model with sparse-MoE architecture, image input support, and a 256K-token context. The document reports agentic coding and vision-to-code evaluations, outlines a multi-stage training pipeline, and gives qualitative safety practices but no numeric safety score table.

capabilities.text: Handles text and image inputs for coding assistance while returning text over a 256K-token context; the summary lists 138B total and 5B active parameters.
Targets Copilot developer workflows such as agentic coding, repository Q&A, refactoring, and tool-using tasks.
Uses supervised tuning, a synthetic agentic phase of about 2 million tasks, and reinforcement learning over more than 150,000 environments after a compressed MAI-Thinking-1 checkpoint.
Adds image-grounded coding evaluations and compares against the earlier MAI-Code-1-Flash release on production-harness tasks.

evaluations.context: VS Code-based production GitHub Copilot harness
Same harness comparison with MAI-Code-1-Flash and other listed models
Vision-to-web coding task with Haiku 4.5 and GPT 5.4 mini comparators

safety_findings.text: Pretraining data handling filters or down-ranks harmful content to reduce exposure during base-model learning.
Supervised tuning and reinforcement learning are described as alignment stages for shaping safer and more helpful behavior.
The card names CyberBench, CyberSecEval, and SecRepo as security-oriented evaluations.
Deployment review used production model APIs with safety classifiers and filters.

limitations.text: Generated code and text may be unreliable, so the card calls for developer review and validation before serious use.
The safety section gives methods and benchmark names but not numeric safety outcomes.
General benchmark coverage is deferred to the prior MAI-Code-1-Flash card.
Client distribution wording differs between a VS Code-focused use-case passage and the later all-clients statement.

practical_implications.text: Use it for repository-aware coding and agentic edits, but verify outputs with tests and code review.
Image input can help with UI and screenshot-driven tasks, yet the vision results show that success is not uniform.
Keep tool permissions constrained and avoid trusting instructions found in untrusted repository content.
Compare against MAI-Code-1-Flash mainly on the reported coding and vision-task deltas, then validate on local workloads.
Consult current Copilot docs for client availability because the card's wording is mixed.

coverage_notes: This digest covers the complete six-page MAI-Code-1.1-Flash card, focusing on technical summary, training, safety notes, and evaluation tables. It avoids administrative contact details and uses MAI-Code-1-Flash only as a comparison baseline.
